label: 510(k) Medical Device — Substantial Equivalence Comparison
description: Predicate comparison and SE determination for NeuroSense Pro vs. NicoletOne cEEG.

inputs.subject_intended_use: Non-invasive recording, display, and storage of EEG signals in adult and pediatric patients (≥2 years) in hospital settings with automated alerting
inputs.predicate_intended_use: Non-invasive recording, display, and storage of EEG signals in adult and pediatric patients in hospital settings
inputs.intended_use_comparison: Same — both intended for in-hospital continuous EEG monitoring. Subject device adds automated alerting as an adjunctive feature.
inputs.subject_indications: Continuous EEG monitoring for seizure detection, status epilepticus monitoring, brain function monitoring in ICU patients
inputs.predicate_indications: Continuous EEG monitoring for seizure detection and brain function monitoring
inputs.indications_comparison: Same core indications — subject device specifies status epilepticus monitoring explicitly
inputs.subject_environment: Hospital — ICU, epilepsy monitoring unit, OR, emergency department
inputs.predicate_environment: Hospital — ICU, epilepsy monitoring unit, OR
inputs.environment_comparison: Same hospital settings; subject adds ED as explicit use environment
inputs.subject_materials: Medical-grade silicone, ABS housing, silver/silver chloride electrodes, silicone headset
inputs.predicate_materials: Medical-grade silicone, ABS housing, gold cup electrodes
inputs.materials_diff: Different electrode material (Ag/AgCl vs. gold cup); equivalent biocompatibility per ISO 10993
inputs.subject_design: 32-channel amplifier, wireless headset, Bluetooth LE data link, ML-assisted processing
inputs.predicate_design: 25-channel amplifier, wired headset, USB data link
inputs.design_diff: More channels (32 vs 25), wireless vs. wired, added ML processing — performance testing demonstrates equivalent signal quality
inputs.subject_energy: Rechargeable Li-ion battery (headset) + AC mains (base station)
inputs.energy_diff: Subject uses battery for headset; IEC 60601-1 compliance demonstrated for both energy sources
inputs.subject_software: Embedded firmware v2.1 + desktop application v4.0; IEC 62304 Class B; ML seizure detection algorithm
inputs.predicate_software: Embedded firmware + desktop application; proprietary signal processing
inputs.software_diff: Subject includes ML-based seizure detection (adjunctive, not diagnostic). Software documented per IEC 62304.
inputs.subject_sterilization: Electrodes: EtO sterilized (disposable). Headset: high-level disinfection.
inputs.predicate_sterilization: Electrodes: EtO sterilized (disposable). Headset: high-level disinfection.
inputs.dimensions_diff: Subject is lighter and more compact due to wireless design; no impact on safety or effectiveness
inputs.perf_criteria_3: ≥ 85% per FDA guidance on Computer-Assisted Detection Devices
inputs.se_determination: The NeuroSense Pro has the same intended use as the predicate device. Technological differences (increased channels, wireless, ML-based seizure detection) do not raise new questions of safety or effectiveness. Performance testing demonstrates that signal quality is equivalent or superior to the predicate. The ML seizure detection feature is adjunctive (not standalone diagnostic) and meets FDA guidance thresholds. The device is substantially equivalent to the predicate.
